reason: Both satisfy the hard requirements (correct headings, snapshot-before-risk, no restart/failover before snapshot, explicit abort/rollback conditions), but Response B is slightly more operationally robust: it embeds distinct abort/rollback conditions in both IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (snapshot failure/timeout) and MITIGATION (stalled recovery after mitigation), gives practical guidance for the edge case where a fully consistent snapshot isn't guaranteed under time pressure, and its FOLLOW UP section is more actionable with owners/due dates and a snapshot-restorability check.
